subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a model-callable, current-session self-compaction action in core, with the narrow `session_status(action: "compact")` boundary proposed by the linked implementation?
rationale: The implementation changes which agent-originated session mutations core permits; source-level correctness cannot decide the intended permanent tool and authorization contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow action
options.body: Adopt the current-session-only action, require a refreshed branch and review of recovery, transcript cleanup, mutation tracking, and permission boundaries.

options.title: Choose another core boundary
options.body: Keep the capability but direct it to a different explicitly owned agent/runtime API rather than extending session_status.

options.title: Decline model-triggered compaction
options.body: Retain automatic, user, and operator compaction only and close the focused implementation with the product rationale.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow action
recommendation.body: Adopt the current-session-only action, require a refreshed branch and review of recovery, transcript cleanup, mutation tracking, and permission boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature history and recent discussion tie this contributor most directly to the existing session-status and compaction boundary.
